skill.name: wechat-mp-content-review
skill.description: Review WeChat Official Account articles with SocialDataX, comparing visible engagement, content themes, and reader feedback from supplied links or account IDs.
skill.summary: Produce evidence-based WeChat article reviews with bounded sampling, explicit data gaps, and up to three editorial recommendations.
skill.author: devinchen2014

security_audit.summary: All 38 static alerts are false positives involving Markdown, declared credential names, boolean-only environment checks, application identifiers, or readable Chinese text. The CLI examples introduce a separate supply-chain risk by automatically executing an unpinned npm package. No evidence found of embedded credentials, credential exfiltration, destructive operations, or prompt injection in the reviewed files; external package implementation was not provided.

remediation.issue: Direct CLI examples execute socialdatax-skills@latest through npx -y without a reviewed version or dependency lock.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed package version and locked dependencies, verify registry integrity and provenance, and require approval before installation or updates.

content.user_title: Review WeChat Articles and Reader Feedback
content.value_statement: WeChat content reviews need reliable comparisons without inventing missing engagement data. This skill organizes SocialDataX lookups into article comparisons, reader evidence, and focused editorial recommendations.
actual_capabilities: Resolve an account from an article link or account ID, and verify account ownership for supplied article lists.
Compare up to 10 articles across at most three account-list pages, removing duplicates and recording coverage limits.
Retrieve visible article statistics, preserve missing values, and calculate ratios only when valid numerator and denominator values exist.
Verify content themes using two or three representative article bodies rather than requiring full text for every sample.
Review comments for up to two articles and retrieve one reply page for one key comment when context is necessary.
Produce an article comparison table, evidence-linked reader feedback, and up to three editorial test recommendations.
limitations: Requires an authenticated SocialDataX connection or API key; direct CLI use also needs Node.js, npm, network access, and approved package execution.
Account reviews cover at most 10 articles and three list pages; a nickname alone cannot identify the target account.
Visible cumulative statistics may be incomplete and cannot establish open rates, completion rates, follower attribution, revenue, or causal effects.
Does not log into account administration, publish articles, reply to readers, send messages, or change account settings.

use_cases.title: Review Recent Editorial Performance
use_cases.description: Compare a bounded article sample, visible engagement, and verified themes before selecting the next editorial tests.

use_cases.title: Prepare an Evidence-Based Client Report
use_cases.description: Review supplied article links with account separation, observation times, missing-data notes, and source-linked recommendations.

use_cases.title: Summarize Reader Questions
use_cases.description: Inspect representative comments and necessary reply context to identify supported questions for future content.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Article
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this WeChat article: [article link]. Report visible statistics, verified content themes, and missing data without inferring unavailable metrics.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: start with a supplied article link.

prompt_templates.title: Compare an Account Sample
prompt_templates.prompt: Review account [account ID] using up to 10 articles and three list pages. Compare themes and visible engagement, recording observation times and coverage limits.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: compare a bounded account sample.

prompt_templates.title: Connect Themes with Reader Feedback
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these articles: [links]. Verify themes with representative bodies and comments from at most two articles. Cite evidence and propose three editorial tests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: combine content evidence with reader responses.

prompt_templates.title: Resume an Incomplete Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Resume [partial review] using [saved pagination token]. Preserve completed results and failures. Deduct consumed pages and articles from the three-page and 10-article limits.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: recover partial results without restarting the sample.

output_examples.input: Review an account sample when some article statistics are unavailable.
output: Illustrative result only: Eight distinct articles were retrieved across two pages; coverage of the latest publications could not be confirmed.
Six articles have visible read counts. Two statistics requests failed and remain marked unavailable, not zero.
Theme comparisons include article counts and valid-statistics counts. Differences in publication age prevent direct causal conclusions.
Next test: Compare two articles with similar publication ages before changing the editorial plan.

output_examples.input: Review a supplied article list when reader comments are unavailable.
output: Illustrative result only: Three supplied articles were compared; two representative bodies were available for theme verification.
Reader feedback: Unavailable because no comments were returned. No audience sentiment conclusion is supported.
Recommendation: Test one verified theme again and gather comment evidence before generalizing reader preferences.
Open rates, completion rates, follower growth, and revenue cannot be calculated from the returned fields.

best_practices: Provide complete article links or an account ID, keep credentials outside chat, and approve a reviewed, pinned CLI version before execution.
Record observation times, publication ages, sample coverage, and missing statistics before comparing engagement.
Support content judgments with article evidence and reader claims with comments; present recommendations as tests rather than proven causes.
anti_patterns: Treating an account nickname as an account ID or combining articles from different accounts into one account review.
Replacing failed statistics with zero or inferring audience sentiment without retrieved comments.
Inferring open rates, completion rates, follower growth, or revenue from public engagement counts.

faq.question: What inputs are required?
faq.answer: Provide an article link, complete share text, an account ID, or up to 10 article links. A nickname alone is insufficient.

faq.question: Do I need a SocialDataX API key?
faq.answer: Direct CLI calls require a runtime API key. An already authenticated hosted MCP connection does not require a separate local CLI variable.

faq.question: What does direct CLI execution require?
faq.answer: It requires Node.js, npm, network access, and package execution permission. The examples use an unpinned npm package; approve a reviewed version first.

faq.question: Can this skill publish articles or reply to readers?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflow retrieves account information, articles, statistics, comments, and replies without modifying the account.

faq.question: How are missing metrics handled?
faq.answer: Missing, null, and failed results remain explicitly marked. Ratios require valid inputs, and unavailable metrics are never replaced with invented values.

faq.question: What happens after rate limits or insufficient balance?
faq.answer: Rate limits pause new requests before resuming unfinished work. Insufficient balance stops further calls while preserving completed results for later continuation.
